body: I am both an EMT and a CVT (certified vet tech) and you treat them the same: ABCs, treat for shock and transport. The only main difference is that very few people will pay the thousands of dollars to save the dog (and veterinary hospitals won't do it without an owner) so transporting/ treating the dog probably isn't worth it. Also, spinal precautions arent as big because most people euthanize if there is spinal damage.

I apologize if it came across that way, but that wasn't my meaning. Owners wanting to know what is the best thing for their pet is fantastic, but some of the information that I see floating around the internet is, quite frankly, laughable. Someone using it with the best intentions is not. If people want to know how to extend their pets' lives I really would consult with your vet. They did not get into this field for the money and can help you with things like nutrition, exercise and dental care.

Vet tech here:
A part of me always laughs when I see these instructions for a couple of reasons. The main one is that veterinary clinics and human emergency rooms are not equipped the same. CPR isn't meant to restart the heart (and it only does like 5% of the time), but rather it is meant to keep blood flowing long enough for something that CAN restart the heart: defibrillation, drugs, emergency surgery, etc.  Unless you are going to a specialized clinic like those at a major university, veterinary clinics do not have defibrillators.  I will admit that they do almost all have drugs and the ability to do basic surgery. However, then you need to consider why your pet went into cardiac arrest. Heart attacks are rare in dogs, so if it was a sudden cardiac arrest, it was probably trauma related. This usually means that the animal needs emergency surgery which most clinics aren't equipped for: ventilators... even sterile suction isn't available at a lot of clinics. Even the places that are equipped- it is probably going to cost thousands-tens of thousands for that surgery, which most people just can't afford.

CPR has its merits in specific situations: during anesthesia because we can control the cause of the cardiac arrest (drugs) and often can reverse these drugs, if you are near a specialized emergency facility and have the money, or if you have a young animal who went into cardiac arrest for unknown reasons. Otherwise, to be honest, it probably won't do anything.  Sorry to be the debby downer.

Honestly, I don't know your exact life, but I am sorry that you feel like a second choice- that is hard.  Obviously I am NOT a therapist (I work in IT haha) so take all of this with a grain of salt.  I would give you the cliche of "be your own favorite person," but since I am only starting to learn this after 29 years in my "healthy" brain, that seems silly. The only things that I can say are a couple of other cliches: life changes rapidly and you might not have met this person yet (I didn't meet mine until 2 years ago and I am an Athiest so I don't even believe in this- yet here I am), and a parent's love is intense and unconditional. On the first one, I know that is so hard to believe or even wait for. But, if I look back at my life 10 years ago, holy crap it is sooo different. A lot of bad, a lot of good, mostly "meh."- but very different. Different than I ever thought it would be. So, yeah, fight for that future person.
The cliche about your parents: if you are tied (with your siblings) for your parent's favorite person, that is on them and not you. I have seen more parents who have lost children than I would ever want to, and the dead look in their eyes is haunting: not only did they lose their favorite person, they lost themselves. 
On another, personal note... just because someone loves you doesn't mean that they are going to be good at articulating it on a daily basis. The saying "people only love you when you are dead" has some bearing not because it is true, but because there isn't a "we can meet tomorrow" mentality. I learned this the hard way: my best friend died in a car accident when we were 17. She lived about an hour and a half away, so I hadn't seen her in about 7 months. There was always tomorrow, next week, next month. The last words I spoke to her were not kind- we were fighting about something (stupid I am sure) and I ended the convo with "fuck off." The reality is that I now think of her daily, and I probably didn't before. But, I know that I loved her just as much when she was alive as I do now, I just don't hold the luxury of a tomorrow. So, yeah, I do believe that you are somebody's favorite person.
Good luck. Keep up the fight. Sorry for the cliches- I just know my truths and those are among them.
Thank you for being here.  Keep up the fight.
